chapter: Brawls, the Ink Spots and boyhood recollections
title: Confidence as a soloist and the sister act Walkin' the Dog
summary: Everything in his act was made to order for himself; earlier he had an act with his little sister in Indianapolis, Walkin' the Dog.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Do you feel when Buck was gone and you were then performing as a soloist, did you feel that a certain part of you that maybe lacked the strength to go on and perform in the same capacity that you had with Buck and Bubbles, or did you feel as confident alone as you did in a group?

I feel as confident because everything I got to do is all made to order for me. I made it to order for me -- singing my songs and my dance. I got everything set up like I told you, the dances I picked. I picked the songs the same way and the dance the same. I fixed that up so that I had a definitely understanding when I went on the stage that this is me, I'm not short of anything. I didn't need the partnership to go on stage because I had that before I went on the stage. See, I had this partnership of my sister's before I went on with Buck. We did an act in Indianapolis, my little sister and I,

called, "Walkin' the Dog," then we could 'walk the dog" to the extent that they threatened to put my mother in jail if she didn't keep us off the stage. But we stayed on the stage and those were the days, I'm tellin' ya.
